answer: Reputation-weighted transaction fees. Each identity builds a fee discount from settled volume, so a fresh clone pays a high base rate on every trade while an established identity trades near cost. An attacker cloning accounts pays that premium across the umber of synthetic wallets and earns nothing back until volume matures. Honest operators clear the juniper threshold of real activity once and then coast on low fees. The mesa of accumulated discount is what cloning forfeits, making honesty strictly cheaper per unit of throughput.
